questions.question: You need to view the available memory and logical disk free space of 30 Azure virtual machines, and a map of the processes that connect to other servers. What should you enable?

options.text: VM insights with processes and dependencies (Map)
options.why: Correct. VM insights collects guest performance data through the Azure Monitor Agent and can collect dependency data for the Map.
Storage insights reports on storage accounts, not virtual machines.
Boot diagnostics captures console output for troubleshooting startup.

options.text: A diagnostic setting on each virtual machine
options.why: Virtual machine diagnostic settings send only host platform metrics, which do not include guest memory or process connections.

questions.explanation: VM insights uses a data collection rule and the Azure Monitor Agent, and stores data in InsightsMetrics and, for Map, VMProcess and VMConnection.

questions.question: You need a view of capacity, transactions, latency and availability across all storage accounts in a subscription. The solution must require no configuration. What should you use?

options.why: Correct. Storage insights is built on platform metrics and is available without setup.
VM insights monitors virtual machines.

options.text: A diagnostic setting on each storage account
options.why: Diagnostic settings require configuration on every account.
Connection monitor tests network connectivity between endpoints.

questions.explanation: Storage insights and Network insights are curated workbooks over platform metrics and resource health.

questions.question: An application on VM1 intermittently fails to connect to a SQL Server instance on VM2 on TCP port 1433. You must continuously test the connection, record the round-trip time and be alerted when checks fail. What should you configure?

options.text: A Connection monitor test group with VM1 as the source, VM2 as the destination and a TCP test on port 1433
options.why: Correct. Connection monitor runs tests at a set frequency, stores results in Log Analytics and can create alerts.
IP flow verify checks a single flow at one point in time.
Next hop shows the route that a packet takes. It does not test continuously.
Packet capture records traffic for analysis but does not alert on failed checks.

questions.explanation: Connection monitor test configurations define the protocol, port, frequency and success thresholds such as checks failed (%) and round-trip time.

questions.question: You need to determine whether inbound TCP traffic on port 3389 from 203.0.113.10 to a virtual machine is allowed, and which network security group rule applies. Which Network Watcher tool should you use?

options.why: Correct. IP flow verify returns Allow or Deny for a flow and names the security rule that made the decision.
Next hop identifies the next hop type and route table, not NSG decisions.
Connection monitor runs ongoing tests but is not the quickest way to name a single blocking rule.
VPN troubleshoot diagnoses VPN gateways and connections.

questions.explanation: NSG diagnostics provides a similar check for wider source and destination inputs.

questions.question: You plan to use an Azure virtual machine named VM1 as a source in Connection monitor. Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: VM1 requires the Network Watcher Agent virtual machine extension
options.why: Correct. Azure virtual machine sources run tests through the Network Watcher Agent extension, which the portal can install.

options.text: Network Watcher must be enabled in the region of VM1
options.why: Correct. Network Watcher is regional and is enabled automatically when a virtual network is created in the region.

options.text: VM1 must have a public IP address
options.why: Connection monitor tests can run between private addresses.

options.text: Test results can be stored in a Log Analytics workspace
options.why: Correct. Results are written to tables such as NWConnectionMonitorTestResult.
The Network Watcher Agent is available for Windows and Linux.

questions.explanation: Connection monitor combines sources, destinations and test configurations in test groups and stores results in Log Analytics.
